answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by requiring every agent to lock a refundable stake before it can earn or vote, like timber piled as collateral before building. New identities start with near-zero weight and gain influence only through consistent, peer-attested work over many epochs, so one operator cannot cheaply spin up an ocean of sock puppets. Each record is crystal clear on the public ledger: misbehavior slashes the stake and burns the reputation built. An attacker must pay a fresh bond per fake identity and lose it when caught — so an attack costs far more than it can earn.
